junction.name: Grand Concourse & East 149 Street, New York City

claims.text: Grand Concourse & East 149 Street had 85 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 19 pedestrians injured, 13 cyclists injured and 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.8 million a year.
25% of crashes here involved a two-wheeler, against 16% at the city's priority junctions.
18% of crashes here had “traffic control disregarded” recorded as a contributing factor, against 3% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading south and a two-wheeler was involved in 15% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 4% at the city's priority junctions (found by the exhaustive search).

Held up on later years: “traffic control disregarded” was recorded and a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading south in 9% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 1% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.6 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $873,000 a year.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 1.3 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $454,000 a year; check on site: the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Grand Concourse, East 149 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 17, New York City Council; Bronx Community Board 1.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 17, New York City Council; Bronx Community Board 1
Subject: Request for safety review at Grand Concourse & East 149 Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We write about the junction of Grand Concourse & East 149 Street.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 157 crashes, of which 85 caused injury, with 19 pedestrians injured, 13 cyclists injured, and 1 person killed. This is a city priority location. In dollar terms, using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the harm is about $5.8 million per year. There is no recorded safety treatment in this period; the latest recorded safety project is a Leading Pedestrian Interval signal in 2013.

For any approach you own (Grand Concourse and East 149 Street), we ask you to carry out a safety study and, where warranted, implement:

* longer yellow signal times (Yellow Change Intervals), expected to prevent about 4.6 injury crashes per year (about $1,583,000 of harm avoided per year; pays for itself if the cost is under $11.1 million);
* reflective backplates on the traffic signals (Backplates with Retroreflective Borders), expected to prevent about 2.6 injury crashes per year (about $873,000 of harm avoided per year; pays for itself if the cost is under $6.1 million).

Please confirm what checks and timing plan you will apply on each road for which you are responsible, and share the study findings.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

- NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (corridors); NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (intersections); NYC Vision Zero View, Enhanced Crossings (6ax4-q5k4); NYC Vision Zero View, Leading Pedestrian Interval Signals; NYC Vision Zero View, Signal Timing/25 MPH Retiming; NYC Vision Zero View, Speed Humps (jknp-skuy); NYC Vision Zero View, Turn Traffic Calming; NYC Vision Zero priority corridors; NYC Vision Zero priority intersections
